requestBody.description:
Request body for creating a task comment (WI-1).

Contains only `content`. `author` is deliberately absent: it is assigned by
the server based on which endpoint is used (public `/tasks/:id/comments` →
`user`, `/tasks/:id/comments/agent` → `agent`), so ordinary clients cannot
impersonate the agent or system (invariant 2).

200.description:
A single entry in a task's comment timeline (WI-1).

Comments are append-only: there is no edit operation, and `author` is
server-assigned when the row is created. `seq` is a per-task monotonic
sequence assigned by storage, so ordering is deterministic even when
multiple rows share a `created_at` timestamp.

200.description:
A scheduled span for a habit (#503).

Its effect depends on `habits.active`:
- `active = true`: the span suppresses task generation (a pause).
- `active = false`: the span enables task generation (an activation window).

`start_date` / `end_date` are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` strings in the
user's local timezone.

requestBody.description:
Query for the memory read auto-injection retrieval path (WI-4 / #1003).

Unlike [`MemoryQuery`] (user-facing keyword search), this is a *reverse*
lookup: memories whose `normalized_key` occurs as a substring of `text`
are candidates, ranked server-side by key specificity and recency. Used at
turn start to surface `proper_noun` / `fact` memories without the agent
calling any search tool.

200.description: Result of a memory read auto-injection retrieval (WI-4 / #1003).

Abandonability.description:
A value in `[0.0, 1.0]` representing how easily a task can be abandoned.

Higher values mean the task is more likely to be dropped when the schedule
does not fit. `new` silently clamps the input to `[0.0, 1.0]`; `NaN`
becomes `0.5`.

CommentAuthor.description:
Author of a task comment (`task_comments` table, WI-1).

`User` is assigned by the public comment endpoint, `Agent` by the
agent-only endpoint, and `System` is created only server-side
(migrations, hooks) — never accepted from any request.

CommentRow.description:
A single entry in a task's comment timeline (WI-1).

Comments are append-only: there is no edit operation, and `author` is
server-assigned when the row is created. `seq` is a per-task monotonic
sequence assigned by storage, so ordering is deterministic even when
multiple rows share a `created_at` timestamp.

label.description: Label shown in the completion UI.

value.description: Full query value after selecting this completion.

CoverageConfirmationRow.description:
A recorded coverage confirmation (WI-10).

Confirms that a local period was covered: the user (or an intake/capture
flow) stated what happened during that interval.

CoverageEvaluation.description: Coverage data assembled for one planner evaluation (WI-10).

unclassified_gaps.description:
Unclassified schedule gaps detected for the current evaluation.
These are synthetic unsettled intervals derived from the active schedule.

CoverageState.description:
Coverage trust state consumed by the resident agent (WI-10).

Precedence is `bootstrap -> stale -> today-covered -> trusted`. A stale
state triggers a settlement prompt; today-covered makes the current task
authoritative; trusted is reached by a target-period procedure.

oneOf.description: No coverage confirmation has been recorded.
Coverage for today has been confirmed.
The coverage record is trusted for the target period.

The coverage is stale: unresolved interval, expired confirmation, or
stale calendar sync.

CreateComment.description:
Request body for creating a task comment (WI-1).

Contains only `content`. `author` is deliberately absent: it is assigned by
the server based on which endpoint is used (public `/tasks/:id/comments` →
`user`, `/tasks/:id/comments/agent` → `agent`), so ordinary clients cannot
impersonate the agent or system (invariant 2).

CreateCoverageConfirmation.description: Request body for recording a coverage confirmation (WI-10).

CreateDevice.description: Request body for registering a new device.

CreateHabitBatchItem.description: A single habit inside a batch create request (#1083).

CreateHabitBatchResult.description: A single result from a batch create request (#1083).

window_mode.description:
Window mode for generated tasks (#window_mode).
`'day'` (default) = occurrence day's start_time..end_time.
`'period'` = occurrence start_time .. next occurrence's start_time.

habit_step_id.description: habit step link (#95). Set by sync_habit_tasks for step-generated tasks.

original_quantity_total.description: WI-9: pre-split total quantity, kept for lineage.

quantity_done.description: WI-9: initial quantity already done (defaults to 0).

quantity_total.description: WI-9: total quantity for a quantitative task.

CreateTaskBatchItem.description:
A single task inside a batch create request (#1083).
`client_id` is a caller-supplied temporary id that can be referenced by
`depends` of other items in the same batch.

habit_step_id.description: habit step link (#95). Set by sync_habit_tasks for step-generated tasks.

original_quantity_total.description: WI-9: pre-split total quantity, kept for lineage.

quantity_done.description: WI-9: initial quantity already done (defaults to 0).

quantity_total.description: WI-9: total quantity for a quantitative task.

CreateTaskBatchResult.description:
A single result from a batch create request (#1083).
The caller can correlate results with input items by `client_id` and by
position.

actual_minutes.description: Total active work minutes from work_sessions (NULL when no work has been done).

completed_at.description: WI-9: wall-clock completion time, set by `complete`.

habit_step_id.description:
The habit step that generated this task, if any (#95). NULL for simple
(step-less) habits and manually created tasks.

original_quantity_total.description: WI-9: pre-split total quantity, kept for lineage.

quantity_done.description: WI-9: quantity already done. Defaults to 0.

quantity_total.description: WI-9: total quantity for a quantitative task (e.g. 30 題).

split_from_task_id.description: WI-9: for a remainder task, the id of the task it was split from.

CreateUnsettledInterval.description: Request body for recording an unsettled interval (WI-10 / WI-18).

Date.description:
A calendar date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format.

Serialized as a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string for JSON and stored as `TEXT` in
SQLite. Wraps [`jiff::civil::Date`].

DeleteAllGcalResult.description: Result of explicitly deleting every mapped Google Calendar event.

Response for `GET /api/tasks/dependency-analysis` and the habit step
variant (#355).

DependencyNode.description: A node on a dependency witness path (task or habit step) (#355).

EvaluationEstimator.description: Estimator distribution snapshot for a single task.

EvaluationInputs.description:
Raw inputs for one consistent planner-event evaluation.

The storage backend collects these in a single atomic read (or as close to
atomic as the backend supports) so the pure evaluator receives a coherent
snapshot. The caller still supplies `now`, gap classification, and coverage.

coverage.description: Coverage trust state for the current evaluation (WI-10).

EvaluationTaskProgress.description:
Per-task progress for evaluation. Only in-progress tasks are included; the
estimator is pre-computed by the storage layer so callers do not have to
re-derive the fallback distribution.

EventDeliveryState.description: Delivery state persisted by the resident event ledger (WI-9).

HabitDetail.description:
Habit detail response: the habit row plus its steps (#95). Used by
`GET /api/habits/:id` so clients receive steps in one round-trip.

window_mode.description:
Window mode for generated tasks (#window_mode).
`'day'` (default) = occurrence day's start_time..end_time.
`'period'` = occurrence start_time .. next occurrence's start_time.

apply.description:
When true, persist the computed `avg_minutes` / `sigma_minutes` to the
habit (and its steps). When false, return a preview only.

detect_outliers.description:
When true, detect and exclude outliers using the median absolute
deviation (MAD) before computing the estimate.

applied.description: True when the result was written back to the habit/steps.

habit.description: The updated habit row, present only when `apply` was true.

samples.description: Task-level samples for non-step habits. Empty for step-based habits.

HabitEstimateSample.description: One completed task observation included in a habit estimate.

HabitEstimateStep.description: Estimate result for a single habit step.

HabitPreviewRequest.description:
Preview request for `POST /api/habits/preview`. Mirrors `CreateHabit`
plus an optional step list and preview range.

HabitPreviewTask.description: A single task occurrence produced by `HabitPreviewRequest`.

window_mode.description:
Window mode for generated tasks (#window_mode).
`'day'` (default) = occurrence day's start_time..end_time.
`'period'` = occurrence start_time .. next occurrence's start_time.

HabitScheduledSpanRow.description:
A scheduled span for a habit (#503).

Its effect depends on `habits.active`:
- `active = true`: the span suppresses task generation (a pause).
- `active = false`: the span enables task generation (an activation window).

`start_date` / `end_date` are inclusive `YYYY-MM-DD` strings in the
user's local timezone.

HabitStepInput.description:
Input element for `PUT /api/habits/:id/steps` (bulk replace, #95).
An `id` present in the DB keeps the existing step (preserving its link to
generated tasks); an `id` absent or unknown creates a new step. Existing
steps not in the array are deleted. `depends_on` references step ids that
must exist in the resulting set.

HabitStepRow.description:
A step of a multi-step habit (#95). Each step produces one task per
occurrence with its own window / cost / flags. Steps form a DAG via
`depends_on` (JSON array of step ids within the same habit).

depends_on.description: JSON array of step ids this step depends on (within the same habit).

JsonString.description:
A wrapper that serializes `T` as a JSON string on the wire and in the DB.

Common instantiations:
- `JsonString<Vec<String>>` — task / step dependency lists
- `JsonString<Vec<ScheduleEntry>>` — schedule entry arrays

JsonString2.description:
A wrapper that serializes `T` as a JSON string on the wire and in the DB.

Common instantiations:
- `JsonString<Vec<String>>` — task / step dependency lists
- `JsonString<Vec<ScheduleEntry>>` — schedule entry arrays

MemoryInjectionQuery.description:
Query for the memory read auto-injection retrieval path (WI-4 / #1003).

Unlike [`MemoryQuery`] (user-facing keyword search), this is a *reverse*
lookup: memories whose `normalized_key` occurs as a substring of `text`
are candidates, ranked server-side by key specificity and recency. Used at
turn start to surface `proper_noun` / `fact` memories without the agent
calling any search tool.

limit.description: Maximum number of memories to return (default 5, capped at 20).

text.description: The raw user utterance. Normalized server-side before matching.

MemoryInjectionResult.description: Result of a memory read auto-injection retrieval (WI-4 / #1003).

counts.description:
Per-kind memory counts so the agent knows whether the store is
non-empty even when no memory matches the utterance.

MemoryKindCounts.description: Total memory rows per kind, used for the system-prompt memory hint.

MemorySource.description:
Provenance of a memory row (see `doc/code-quality-issues.md` §34).

Matches the `memories.source` CHECK constraint in
`migrations/016_memory.sql`: `user_confirmed`, `agent_inferred`,
`imported`. Currently only `UserConfirmed` is written by the storage
layer, but the schema accepts all three so the enum keeps them as
variants to round-trip existing rows safely.

Quantity.description:
A non-negative integer quantity.

Negative values are rejected at construction time. The inner `i64` can be
retrieved via [`Quantity::get`].

RedundantDependency.description:
A redundant (composite / transitively implied) dependency edge with a
witness path proving the direct edge is unnecessary (#355).

RefreshEvaluatorHeartbeat.description: Request body for refreshing a desktop evaluator heartbeat.

RefreshEvaluatorLease.description: Request body for reserving or renewing an Android evaluator lease.

ResidentAuthority.description: Result of resolving which device currently holds resident authority.

device_id.description:
The resident device, or `None` when no device currently holds a valid
evaluator heartbeat or lease.

is_resident.description: `true` when the requesting `candidate_id` is the resident authority.

next_eval_at.description:
The next scheduled evaluation time advertised by the resident device,
when known.

ScheduleMode.description:
Reschedule / preview mode for schedule operations.

`Range` replans tasks within a time window; `Tasks` replans a specific
set of task IDs; `Full` regenerates the entire schedule (only valid for
preview — `reschedule` rejects it). Used by `Reschedule`,
`SchedulePreviewRequest`, and the CLI's `ScheduleCommands::Reschedule`.

comfortable_minutes.title: 459: 1 日の快適な作業時間（分）。`None` または `0` の場合はデフォルトを使う。

device_priority.description: デバイス優先度リスト。既定は desktop > android。

maximum_minutes.title: 459: 1 日の最大作業時間（分）。`None` または `0` の場合はデフォルトを使う。

plan_length_days.description: スケジュール計画の期間（日数）。horizon 計算に使う。デフォルト 14。

seed.description: 乱数シード。`None` の場合は決定的なデフォルト。

solver.description: 使用する solver。`"sa"` / `"priority"` / `"auto"`。未設定の場合は `sa`。未知値はエラー。

time_budget_ms.description: 求解時間の上限（ミリ秒）。`None` または `0` の場合は制限なし。

warm_start.description: 前回スケジュールから priority/ALNS の初期解を warm start する。

Similarity.description:
A similarity score pairing a metric with a numeric value.

Serialized as `{"metric":"dice","score":0.85}`. Implements [`Default`]
(`Dice`, `0.0`) so it can be used with `#[sqlx(skip)]` / `#[serde(default)]`
on row structs where the SQL/JSON result does not include the field.

SimilarityMetric.description:
Similarity metric used by `Similarity` (see `doc/code-quality-issues.md` #33).

Kept in `takusu-types` so `takusu-contracts`, `takusu-client`, and
`takusu-worker` can all use it without changing the crate dependency
graph.

SleepInput.description:
Sleep configuration for schedule generation / reschedule / preview.

Parsed at the API/CLI boundary from a plain string; consumed by
`takusu-local-lib` to build a `SleepConfig` using settings + timezone.

Solver.description:
Phase 5 solver label (see `doc/type-safety-issues.md` §3.3).

Kept in `takusu-types` because `takusu-core` does not depend on `serde`,
and `takusu-contracts` / `takusu-client` / `takusu-worker` all depend on `takusu-types`.

SpeechCapability.description: Current speech capability for a device.

end_at.description: Optional deadline for the remainder (defaults to the original end_at).

retained_quantity.description: Quantity to keep on the original task.

set_dependency.description: If true, make the remainder depend on the original task.

title.description: Optional title for the remainder (defaults to the original title).

actual_minutes.description: Total active work minutes from work_sessions (NULL when no work has been done).

completed_at.description: WI-9: wall-clock completion time, set by `complete`.

habit_step_id.description:
The habit step that generated this task, if any (#95). NULL for simple
(step-less) habits and manually created tasks.

original_quantity_total.description: WI-9: pre-split total quantity, kept for lineage.

quantity_done.description: WI-9: quantity already done. Defaults to 0.

quantity_total.description: WI-9: total quantity for a quantitative task (e.g. 30 題).

split_from_task_id.description: WI-9: for a remainder task, the id of the task it was split from.

TaskStatus.description:
Phase 1 type-safe labels (see `doc/type-safety-issues.md` §3.1 / 3.2 / 3.5 / 3.6).

These are intentionally kept in `takusu-types` so that `takusu-contracts`,
`takusu-client`, and `takusu-worker` can all use them without changing the
crate dependency graph.

TimeOfDay.description:
A time of day in `HH:MM` format with minutes snapped to 5-minute slots.

Serialized as a `"HH:MM"` string for JSON and stored as `TEXT` in SQLite.
This type was originally defined in `takusu-habit` and has been moved here
so that `takusu-contracts` / `takusu-client` / `takusu-worker` can use it
without depending on `takusu-habit`.

Timestamp.description:
An RFC 3339 timestamp.

Serialized as an RFC 3339 string for JSON and stored as `TEXT` in SQLite.
Wraps [`jiff::Timestamp`].

UndoWorkSessionResult.description:
Response from `POST /api/work-sessions/undo` (WI-14).
`action` is `"deleted"` for a start-undo and `"reopened"` for a pause-undo.

UnsettledIntervalRow.description: An unresolved elapsed-time interval that needs settlement (WI-10 / WI-18).

UpdateDevice.description: Request body for updating a registered device.

color_id.description: `None` = 更新しない、`Some(None)` = クリア、`Some(Some(v))` = 値を設定。

reminder_minutes.description: `None` = 更新しない、`Some(None)` = クリア、`Some(Some(v))` = 値を設定。

transparency.description: `None` = 更新しない、`Some(None)` = クリア、`Some(Some(v))` = 値を設定。

visibility.description: `None` = 更新しない、`Some(None)` = クリア、`Some(Some(v))` = 値を設定。

comfortable_minutes.title: 459: 1 日の快適な作業時間（分）。`None` または `0` の場合はデフォルトを使う。

device_priority.description: デバイス優先度リスト。`None` の場合は更新しない。

maximum_minutes.title: 459: 1 日の最大作業時間（分）。`None` または `0` の場合はデフォルトを使う。

plan_length_days.description: スケジュール計画の期間（日数）。

seed.description: 乱数シード。`None` でデフォルト。

time_budget_ms.description: 求解時間の上限（ミリ秒）。`None` または `0` で制限なし。

warm_start.description: 前回スケジュールから priority/ALNS の初期解を warm start する。

original_quantity_total.description: WI-9: pre-split total quantity, kept for lineage.

quantity_total.description: WI-9: total quantity for a quantitative task.

event.description:
The recorded event, or `None` when the reported quantity_done has not
changed (no-op).

suggests_completion.description: True when the reported quantity_done reaches or exceeds the task total.

WorkSessionRow.description:
A top-level work session. It may be linked to a task, or it may be a
standalone session that is later converted into a task.

Action.description: A single quick action on a check-in or card.

capability.description:
The server-issued one-shot capability for this action, if it is an
immediate capability-authorized action. `Panel` and `Approval` actions
do not carry a capability.

note.description: Note to attach with progress, present for `progress` capabilities.

quantity_total.description: Total quantity for the task/session, present for `progress` capabilities.

request.description:
The original request the capability was minted from.

Included so a client can return the capability unchanged across server
restarts, when the in-memory `CapabilityStore` is empty. The server
ignores this field during authorization; all authoritative parameters
live as top-level fields on the capability itself.

scheduled_at.description:
The scheduled delivery time for notification capabilities (WI-4).

When present, the server derives a longer expiry that covers the
scheduled time plus a short grace period, so the action remains usable
when the notification fires while the app is not in the foreground.

snooze_minutes.description: Snooze duration in minutes, present for `delay` capabilities.

snooze_target.description: Target `start_at` for `delay` capabilities, computed client-side or on first tap (WI-4).

task_id.description: The task this capability is authorized to act on.

ActionGroup.description: One labelled group of actions. Never empty.

session_id.description:
The agent session that will own the pending approval for non-immediate
quick actions. Required when the action resolves to `ChangeProposal`.

CapabilityRequest.description: Request to mint a quick-action capability.

input_path.description:
Trusted input path the client wants the capability to be issued for.

The server minting endpoint decides the actual `input_path` using this
value when present and falling back to a per-endpoint default otherwise.
The client cannot self-assert an arbitrary path: the mint response always
carries the server-chosen path.

scheduled_at.description:
The scheduled delivery time for notification capabilities (WI-4).

When present, the server derives a longer expiry that covers the
scheduled time plus a short grace period, so the action remains usable
when the notification fires while the app is not in the foreground.

ChangeOperation.description: Operation kind for a proposed or applied change.

CheckInCard.description:
A one-round-trip check-in that always offers 「行動」 and 「ズラす」.

The non-empty wrapper on both action groups makes a card without either
group unrepresentable, which enforces the product invariant that every
proactive contact offers both options.

ErrorResponse.description: Default error body returned by agent endpoints.

FocusedQuestion.description: A focused clarification question instead of a full interview.

InputPath.description:
Trusted input path for an action. The server, not the client, decides the
path based on how the capability was issued.

IntakeStage.description: Where the user is in the fixed-order intake interview.

oneOf.description: Interview has not started.
Collecting deadlines and imminent tasks.
Collecting recurring commitments.
Confirming calendar import.
The user paused or finished the interview.

IntakeState.description: Saved state for an interruptible intake interview.

collected_ids.description:
Display ids of tasks/habits created so far in this intake. Used to
resume the summary and avoid re-asking about items already accepted.

coverage_pending.description:
Whether a coverage confirmation is waiting for the current batch to be
committed before it can be recorded.

proposal_id.description:
`proposal_id` used to batch the current set of intake proposals so they
can be approved together.

LlmProviderKind.description:
Identifies which LLM backend implementation to build.

Currently only `OpenAICompatible` exists — OpenAI, OpenRouter, and custom
OpenAI-compatible endpoints are all served by [`OpenAIClient`]. The enum
is kept as a single variant so that future non-OpenAI-compatible providers
(e.g. Anthropic native, Gemini) can be added without touching the dispatch
sites that call [`build_llm_client`].

The legacy `openai`, `openrouter`, and `custom` values (from the previous
three-variant enum) are accepted as aliases during deserialization so that
existing `agent.toml` files and persisted mobile settings keep working.
They all map to `OpenAICompatible`. Serialization always emits
`openai_compatible`.

OkResponse.description: Generic `{ "ok": true }` body used by several agent endpoints.

PendingCheckIn.description:
A task completion that deviated beyond 1σ, awaiting a single check-in
question on the next turn. The user's answer is stored as a task comment.

This is the "next-turn prompt note" delivery mechanism for the overrun
check-in (WI-3); the resident-agent event channel is future work.

delivered.description:
Whether the overrun check-in has ever been surfaced in a system prompt.

A check-in is only treated as answered when a comment is recorded for
the task *after* it has been delivered; comments added before delivery
(e.g. an unrelated note) do not clear it.

Permissions.description:
Permission map for auto-approving proposed changes.

Serialized as a flat map of `"target:operation"` -> bool so that mobile
clients can send it directly without wrapping it in an `allow` field.
Internally the keys are typed (`PermissionKey`) to prevent typos and avoid
per-lookup string allocation.

PlannerEvent.description:
Lightweight event broadcast on the agent transport so surfaces can refresh
when planner state changes (WI-3). Slow subscribers can lag behind up to the
channel capacity; a new subscriber starts from the next event after it
connects, so clients should still refresh once on mount.

kinds.description:
What categories of state may have changed. Clients use this as a hint
when they can refresh selectively; a full refresh is always safe.

Presentation.description:
The typed presentation payload carried on a turn result or event.

Wire form is internally tagged by `type`; unknown tags decode as
[`Presentation::Text`].

oneOf.description: Current + next task with quick actions.
Start / pause / progress / complete / delay / split result.
Schedule read summary.
Task-count read summary.
Conflict / overdue / generation failure.
One-round-trip check-in with 行動 + ズラす.
An approval request, rendered from the existing type.
A focused clarification.

Free-form fallback text.

Represented as a struct variant so internally-tagged serialization works
(serde cannot tag a primitive newtype like `Text(String)`), and so an
unknown tag can degrade to `Text { text }`.

ProgressSummary.description: Aggregated progress counts from a task read.

injected_memory_ids.description:
Memory ids already injected into the system context, so a resumed
session does not re-inject them (WI-4 / #1003).

pending_check_ins.description:
Pending overrun check-ins awaiting an answer (WI-3). Restored so the
check-in is not lost across CLI save/resume.

ScheduleAlert.description: A planner error surfaced to the user (never a check-in).

ScheduleSummary.description: Concise summary of the active schedule.

SettlementPrompt.description:
Settlement prompt shown ahead of the current task when coverage is stale.

Mirrors a one-round-trip check-in so the same action rendering code can
handle it.

SseEvent.description: A server-sent event payload emitted by the agent turn streams.

StartTimeNotification.description: A local notification to post at a task's start time.

check_in.description: The `CheckInCard` presentation rendered for this task.

scheduled_at.description: When the notification should be delivered.

StartTimeNotificationList.description:
Response body for the start-time notification endpoint.

`Versioned<Vec<_>>` cannot be flattened by serde, so the list is wrapped in
a struct.

StartTimeNotificationRequest.description: Request body for the start-time notification endpoint.

device_id.description: Device identifier bound into the issued capabilities.

limit.description: Maximum number of upcoming start-time notifications to return.

tz.description:
IANA or fixed-offset time zone used to format wall-clock times in
notification bodies. Defaults to UTC.

operation_id.description:
Identifies the current device-local turn or audio operation. A late
callback for an older operation is ignored by the state machine.

TargetKind.description: Target kind for a proposed or applied change.

TaskAuthority.description:
Coverage authority attached to a current-task card.

Until WI-10 derives it from observed coverage state, cards default to
[`TaskAuthority::Candidate`] (the safe side of the coverage invariant).

oneOf.description: Present as a candidate for the user to accept (bootstrap).
Authoritative 「今やること」 because today is covered.

TaskCard.description: Current + next task card with quick actions.

settlement.description: Settlement prompt shown before this task when coverage is stale (WI-10).

TtsBlockEvent.description: A TTS block event emitted by the agent turn streams.

TurnEvent.description: Events emitted while a streaming turn is in progress.

oneOf.description: Partial or final ASR transcript captured while the user is speaking.

intake_state.description: Resumable intake interview state at the end of the turn (WI-16).

presentation.description:
Typed presentation derived from the turn's tool results (WI-1). `None`
when no tool result maps to a presentation kind.

WorkState.description: State of a task's work session shown on a card.

WorkTransition.description: Result of a start / pause / progress / complete / delay / split mutation.

detail.description: Human-readable detail (e.g. new quantity, total active minutes).

WorkTransitionKind.description: Kind of a recorded work transition.

oneOf.description:
Emitted by the `ChangeOperation::Snooze` tool for short snoozes
(WI-2 delay) and by quick-action capabilities that perform a short delay.
